We got no templates matching those criteria directly. Maybe need to broaden criteria. The reaction is carbonyl-ene intramolecular forming a five-membered ring (likely a cyclic product). The target molecule is given with mapping numbers. Let's examine the SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Interpretation: There's an alkene CH2= C attached to aromatic ring (c1... phenyl). Also attached to C2 is the rest: chiral carbon 9 attached to a cyclobutane? Actually C9 is attached to a 5-membered ring: C9 attached to CH2-CH2-CH2-C13 (which is chiral) forming a 5-membered ring (maybe a cyclopentane). C13 has OH and CF3 group (C15 with three Fs). So the product is a cyclic ether? Wait OH is attached to C13, not part of ring? The OH is attached to C13 as substituent. The reaction described: carbonyl-ene forms new C-C bond and new hydroxyl (from carbonyl oxygen). So the precursor likely had a carbonyl (ketone) and an alkene in same molecule, which undergoes ene reaction to give a cyclic alcohol (five-membered). So the product we have is the cyclic alcohol (with OH). The precursor would have a carbonyl (C=O) at position of C13? Actually after reaction, the carbonyl becomes OH attached to C13, and the double bond becomes single bond between C1 and C2? Wait the double bond originally is CH2= C (C2). In product, that double bond is gone (C-C single). The carbonyl is gone, replaced by OH on C13. So the precursor likely had a carbonyl at C13 (C=O) and an alkene at C1=C2. The ene reaction forms a new C-C bond between the allylic carbon (C13?) and the alkene carbon (C2?). The new stereocenter at C13 becomes OH.

Thus we need a template for carbonyl-ene intramolecular forming 5-membered ring. Let's search without functional groups criteria, maybe just bonds changed. Use bonds_broken and bonds_formed. Bonds broken: C=C double bond, C=O double bond. Bonds formed: C-C single bond (new), C-O single bond (new). Also maybe bond order changed: C=C to C-C (order change). Let's try search with bonds_broken: ["C=C","C=O"], bonds_formed: ["C-C","C-O"], limit 20.
